title: The affine blowup algebra of a domain in an ideal at a nonzero element is again a domain
author: The Stacks Project Authors

difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for a domain R, an ideal I and a nonzero element a of I, the affine blowup algebra R[I/a] is again a domain (statement lines 17539-17543). The proof does not construct an embedding of R[I/a] into a known domain: it takes two general elements in the fractional form x/a^n and y/a^m supplied by the description of the blowup algebra, clears denominators to reach the relation a^N x y = 0 in R, and uses that R is a domain together with a being nonzero to kill a factor (proof lines 17545-17550). The clearing of denominators, which is what converts a vanishing product in the blowup algebra into a statement about R, is the step that carries the content. H2.
